install.title: Install FM View Exporter
install.intro: We recommend <link>FM View Exporter</link>. It exports any player list in FM27 (squad, player database or shortlist) to CSV with one key press, and it ships with BepInEx, so there is nothing else to install. It needs FM27 on Steam and Windows 10 or 11.
install.setupDownload: Download {file} from the Releases page and run it.
install.setupFind: It finds FM27 in your Steam libraries. If it doesn't, pick the folder that contains {file}.
install.setupInstall: Keep the output format on CSV and the CSV style on the default comma separator, then click Install.
install.setupUpdate: To update later, run the new setup and click Update. Your settings are kept.
install.manualDownload: Download {file} from the Releases page and open your FM27 installation folder:
install.manualSteam: Steam: Right-click FM27 → Manage → Browse local files
install.manualExtract: Extract the contents of the ZIP (not the ZIP itself) into that folder. It should look like:
install.firstLaunch: Start FM27. The first launch takes a few minutes while BepInEx sets itself up; later starts are normal speed. To check the plugin loaded, open this file in the game folder and look for a line mentioning <sb>FM View Exporter</sb>:

export.open: Open your FM27 save and go to Recruitment → Player Database (a squad or shortlist works too)
export.filter: Filter the list down to the players you want. The exporter takes every row in the list, not just the ones on screen.
export.press: Press <sb>F9</sb> and don't click anything until it finishes. The plugin scrolls the list itself; large searches can take a few minutes.

fm27.pickFile: Pick the newest file, e.g. {file}, and import.

help.title: Troubleshooting
help.f9: Check {file} in the game folder. “No player list found” means no player table was open when you pressed F9.
help.start: Rename or delete {file} in the game folder to start without mods, or uninstall with the setup program. Your saves are not affected.
help.antivirus: Some virus scanners flag the setup because it isn't code-signed yet and installs BepInEx. Use the manual ZIP install if you prefer.

use.title: How to use the player list
use.intro: Players lets you import a player export and instantly rank players by a weighted average of their FM26 attributes. No baseline required: just import and score.

download.title: 1. Download a view
download.intro: Download a view and place it in your FM26 or FM27 views folder:
download.more: See the <link>setup guide</link> for full exporter install instructions for each game version.

export.title: 2. Export players from FM
export.open: Open your save and go to Recruitment → Player Database
export.importView: Right-click a column header → Import View and load the view
export.selectView: Select the view from the Custom Views dropdown
export.press: Select the players you want, then press <sb>F9</sb>

import.title: 3. Import the CSV
import.goTo: Go to Players, click Choose CSV file, and navigate to your exporter's output folder:
import.after: Players are scored and sorted immediately after import.

tune.title: 4. Tune weights and columns
tune.body: Click Weights to open Settings at the weights and set how much each attribute counts. The player list re-ranks live next to it. Click Columns to choose which attributes are highlighted in the table. Both, and the attribute colours, are also under the Settings button at the top.

compare.title: 5. Compare players
compare.body: Tick two or more players in the list and click Compare selected to open a side-by-side attribute breakdown view.

math.title: How players are scored
math.intro: Scout Reporter scores players using a weighted average of their raw FM26 attribute values (1–20 scale), then normalises that average to a 100-point scale.

weighted.title: Weighted attribute average
weighted.body: For each attribute you assign a weight (0 = ignore, higher = more important). The score is the weighted mean of all attribute values across every attribute with a non-zero weight. Each profile picks a weighting:
weighted.modes: Linear is how the FM27 benchmarks were calibrated and is the default for new profiles. Emphasized squares weights so doubling a weight more than doubles its influence; profiles made before this option keep it.

benchmarks.title: FM27 benchmark profiles
benchmarks.body: The weights come with six role profiles (Centre-back, Full-back / Wing-back, Defensive / Central midfielder, Attacker / Winger (10), Striker (9) and Goalkeeper) built from <study>FM Match Lab's Study 13b</study>, which measured what one level of each attribute is worth in each position over 50,000 FM27 matches. Each role keeps the attributes the study confirms, scaled so the most valuable one weighs 10: pace and acceleration everywhere, jumping reach mostly for centre-backs and strikers, finishing and strength for forwards, agility and reflexes for keepers. Most technical and mental attributes barely register in the study, so the roles leave them out. Purity's <arena>FM-Arena position test</arena> on another tactic finds the same pattern. The study's Catenaccio run and harvestgreen22's <tactics>test across four tactics</tactics> (1.05 million matches) rank the attributes nearly the same, with only pace, stamina and agility depending on the shape, so one set of weights serves every formation. <update>Match Lab's Study 30</update> found that FM27 27.1 barely changed results, so the study still applies, though passing and shooting attributes may shift a little. Before v1.24 the roles used <scoring>fm-scoring</scoring>'s FM27 weights, which still supply the vs Age table. Edit them freely; “Reset to benchmark” restores the originals.

vsAge.title: vs Age and Potential
vsAge.vsAge: vs Age divides the weighted average by the FM27 benchmark for the player's age (10.3 at 15 up to 13.8 at 24+). 100% means on track to be a high-end Championship / low-end Premier League player in their prime.
vsAge.potential: With a Hidden Attributes export a Potential column appears: the same score using attributes projected to PA. How the potential estimate works explains the projection.

grades.title: Grades
grades.body: Every score gets a letter stamp, FM-style from A+ down to F, plus S, S+ and S++ above A+ for the truly elite. Grades read the weighted average on the 1–20 scale and step every 0.5. The prime benchmark (13.8, a high-end Championship / low-end Premier League player in their prime) is a {grade}. Young players grade low on Now and high on Potential, so compare them with the Potential stamp or vs Age.

normalisation.title: 100-point normalisation
normalisation.body: The weighted average sits on the FM 1–20 attribute scale. It is normalised so that a weighted average of <sb>13</sb> (considered a solid professional) maps to exactly <sb>100</sb>. Scores above 100 indicate above-average players for your weight profile; below 100 means below average.

categories.title: Attribute categories
categories.body: Attributes are grouped into four categories (Technical, Mental, Physical and Goalkeeping), matching FM26's own groupings. You can weight attributes from any category in the same profile, so a goalkeeper weight set can include physical and mental attributes alongside GK-specific ones.

detail.title: Player detail & comparison
detail.body: Clicking a player opens their full attribute sheet with colour-coded values (excellent / good / average / low) based on your theme settings. The compare view places two or more players side-by-side with differences highlighted, making it easy to spot where one player outperforms another for your specific role needs.

export.title: 1. Export with the Hidden Attributes view
export.body: Import the Hidden Attributes view in FM and export as usual. It adds the hidden Professionalism, CA and PA. Standard view exports, or players without CA/PA, are still scored on their current attributes.

import.title: 2. Import and sort
import.body: Import it on Players and sort by Potential (the score at full potential on the weight profile you picked) or vs Age (how far ahead of their age they are now).

inspect.title: 3. Inspect a prospect
inspect.body: Click a player and switch to Full potential to see the estimated attributes at PA, with the gain per attribute. The Development plan below suggests the individual focus, training role, development sessions and coaches that get the most out of them.

ca.title: CA is a cost-weighted attribute sum
ca.body: Each attribute point costs a position-specific amount of CA (fm-scoring's FM27 CA cost table, e.g. Decisions 10 and Agility 8 for a keeper). On a Hidden Attributes export of 109 keepers, CA fits the cost-weighted sum almost exactly (r = 0.99, error ≈ 2.5 CA). The fit is recalibrated on every import that has CA.

growth.title: Spreading the growth
growth.body: The extra points are spread over attributes that can still grow, each in proportion to its room below 20 and to how fast it grew in harvestgreen22's FM27 training test (an 18-year-old training for a season, collected in fm-scoring). Defenders, wing-backs and DMs grow like the defensive ball work schedules, central midfielders like a mix, and wide players, AMs and strikers like the attacking ball work schedules. Keepers weren't tested: their goalkeeping-coached attributes grow at the outfield coached rate. Physicals slow down after 21 (¾ rate to 24, then 0.4), three years later for keepers. Determination, Aggression, Bravery and the keeper tendencies stay put, and outfielders never grow goalkeeping attributes. Multi-position players use the average cost and growth of their positions.

reading.title: Reading the numbers
reading.body: Now and Potential are the best FM27 benchmark role score (1–20). vs Prime compares the potential score to 13.8, the fully developed benchmark. It is an estimate of the ceiling: professionalism, minutes and training decide how much of PA a player reaches.
